title: places through the gazetteers that know them
line: where the geocoder leaves a German, Silesian or Irish string open, GOV or Wikidata is asked and each candidate checked on every part of the string; a Silesian village by its German name resolves to today's place through the one GOV candidate and its geocoder twin, with GOV's dated names; Berthelsdorf stays a card with every candidate offered, a stated Kreis narrowing them; an Irish townland resolves when the string names its county and stays a card with its namesakes when it does not

steps.say: the seed's Silesian birthplace by its German name, as the owner's records write it
the seed's two strings for the Schwenkfelder exiles' Berthelsdorf, one naming Saxony alone, one naming the Kreis Freiberg too
the harness's Irish townland with its county named; the harness file's own string names Ireland alone
the resolver run with the geocoder's, GOV's and Wikidata's real answers planted in their caches

expect.why: to the geocoder the string is a bare name, its one answer Dłużec (old name Langneundorf); GOV's one candidate verifies on the name and on Silesia, and the geocoder answer's SIMC is GOV's own for it, so that answer places it
today's place in today's hierarchy, with GOV's id and its German name until 1945 as a dated name
the overrides hold this string for the owner's review, and several Berthelsdorfs verify besides
the Herrnhut Berthelsdorf is offered, verified on Saxony and Germany; the geocoder's answer for it carries no GOV id, so it stands on its own
so is another Saxon Berthelsdorf: several verify, and the owner chooses
the Berthelsdorf near Freiberg is offered on the geocoder's own entry for it, its twin by the GOV id Wikidata gives that entry's item
a Silesian Berthelsdorf never in Saxony is offered unverified
the overrides hold this string for the owner's review
the Kreis the string states narrows GOV's candidates to the Berthelsdorf that lay in the Amtshauptmannschaft Freiberg
the Herrnhut Berthelsdorf, which the overrides' note suspects, never lay in Freiberg
with its county named the geocoder's unique full match accepts the townland; no gazetteer is asked
the townland in Killeagh, County Cork
with no county named, four townlands verify
Wikidata's candidates are offered on the geocoder's own entries for them, the Tipperary namesake among them
and the Cork townland, the one its county names
Ballyquirk Castle, which Wikidata's search also finds, is not a place of the name and is not offered
every Wikidata candidate is one of the geocoder's own, so none stands on its own

steps.say: the owner chooses, on the Freiberg string's card, GOV's own Erzgebirge village, which the geocoder does not know: a place of its own under Germany

expect.why: the words now mean the place chosen
a place of its own name under Germany, carrying GOV's id, its position and GOV's names of it
